content.title: About
content.content: Dried figs are the dehydrated fruits of the common fig tree (Ficus carica), cultivated in warm regions of the Mediterranean, the Middle East, and California. They have a sweet, slightly caramel-like flavor and a soft, chewy texture. Dried figs are often enjoyed as a snack, added to baked goods, muesli, salads, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: When stored in an airtight container in a cool, dry place, dried figs can keep for up to a year.
Fig cultivation dates back more than 6,000 years, with evidence from ancient Mesopotamia.
Because of their natural sugars, dried figs are frequently used as a natural sweetener.
In ancient Egypt, figs were a symbol of fertility and featured in religious rituals.
The fiber content of dried figs is higher than fresh figs due to moisture removal.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dried figs provide about 9 g of dietary fiber per 100 g, supporting healthy digestion and satiety.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: They contain potassium, magnesium, calcium, and iron, which are essential for muscle, nerve, and blood health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Figs are a good source of polyphenols such as resveratrol and quercetin, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly
items.content: Potassium and fiber in figs may help lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Natural source of sugars
items.content: The fructose and glucose in dried figs provide quick energy, useful for athletes and people with high energy needs.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Dried figs are rich in natural sugars, so individuals with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Fig allergy
items.content: Some people may experience allergic reactions to figs, ranging from skin rash to swelling or breathing difficulties.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Figs contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Commercially packaged figs may contain added sugar or preservatives; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried figs can be eaten straight as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, oatmeal, baked goods, salads, or used in sauces and spreads. Soaking them in warm water can re‑hydrate them slightly for use in desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried figs in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent spoilage and flavor loss.

content.title: About
content.content: Muscle Milk Light is a ready‑to‑drink protein shake designed to support muscle recovery and maintain energy levels. It contains high‑quality whey protein, low fat and carbohydrate content, and added vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The product is based on whey protein, which is rapidly absorbed by the body.
The Light version has roughly half the calories of the regular Muscle Milk.
It uses artificial sweeteners to reduce sugar without sacrificing taste.
Each serving provides about 20 g of protein, meeting most athletes' post‑workout needs.
Packaging is made from recyclable plastic, reducing environmental impact.

items.title: Supports muscle recovery
items.content: Rich whey protein promotes muscle protein synthesis after exercise.

items.title: Low in fat and sugar
items.content: Suitable for calorie‑ and carbohydrate‑restricted diets, helping weight management.

items.title: Vitamin‑mineral complex
items.content: Includes calcium, vitamin D and magnesium, supporting bone health and nervous system function.

items.title: Convenient consumption
items.content: Ready‑to‑drink format requires no preparation, ideal for travel and work.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Contains electrolytes that help maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although the protein is partially hydrolyzed, the drink may still contain lactose, causing discomfort for sensitive individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to whey protein should avoid this product.

items.title: Artificial sweeteners
items.content: Some consumers may be sensitive to sucralose or acesulfame‑K.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Those monitoring salt intake should check daily limits.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Shake the bottle well before drinking and consume immediately after a workout or as a snack between meals. Do not heat the drink.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, refrigerate and consume within 48 hours.

content.title: About
content.content: Pad Thai with chicken is a popular Thai dish made from rice noodles stir‑fried with chicken breast, egg, tofu, bean sprouts, peanuts, and aromatic spices. The sauce typically combines tamarind, fish sauce, sugar and lime, giving the dish a sweet‑sour flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the 1930s in Bangkok as a quick street‑food snack.
It is traditionally served with a lime wedge, fresh cilantro and extra crushed peanuts.
Tamarind, the key ingredient of the sauce, comes from the Tamarindus indica tree, native to Africa but widely cultivated in Southeast Asia.
Original recipes use rice noodles about 5 mm wide, though variations use thicker or thinner noodles.
Pad Thai is often considered Thailand’s “national dish,” despite many regional variations.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken breast and tofu provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Rice noodles supply slowly digestible carbohydrates that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The tamarind‑fish sauce blend contains vitamin B6, which supports protein metabolism and nerve function.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Peanuts and a modest amount of vegetable oil deliver monounsaturated fats beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Lime and cilantro are rich in vitamin C and polyphenols that combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts used in the dish can trigger severe allergic reactions in susceptible individuals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Fish sauce and soy sauce can add a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in soy sauce
items.content: Traditional soy sauce may contain gluten; gluten‑free alternatives should be used for celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The oil and peanuts make the dish relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve Pad Thai hot, garnished with a lime wedge, fresh cilantro and a sprinkle of crushed peanuts. Add chili sauce to taste if you like heat. It is typically eaten with a fork or chopsticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Pad Thai is best enjoyed fresh. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. When reheating, add a splash of water to keep the noodles from drying out.

content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn is whole corn kernels that explode when heated, creating a light, airy snack. Plain ready‑to‑eat popcorn contains no additives, flavorings or salt, preserving the natural taste of corn.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn is the only type of corn whose kernels can “pop” under heat.
The first commercial popcorn appeared in the United States in the late 19th century.
In the US, popcorn is the classic movie‑theater snack.
Popcorn can be prepared in a microwave, on the stovetop, or in a dedicated popcorn maker.
There are more than 30 corn varieties, but only about 5 % are suitable for popcorn.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Plain ready‑to‑eat popcorn provides about 380 kcal per 100 g, which is lower than most crackers and chips.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Popcorn is a good source of dietary fiber, supporting digestive health and promoting satiety.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols in popcorn help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Popcorn naturally contains no gluten, making it suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn provides thiamine, niacin and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Large portions can quickly raise carbohydrate intake, which may be a concern for diabetics.

items.title: Burn risk
items.content: Hot popcorn can burn the mouth and lips, so let it cool slightly before eating.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: While this product is plain, always check labels for hidden flavorings or salt in other brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Popcorn is convenient as a standalone snack, mixed with dried fruit and nuts, or used in recipes such as salads or as a crunchy coating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store popcorn in an airtight container in a dry, cool place away from moisture. For extended shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent staleness.
